BiblicalUsage: Yâla means to speak rashly, to swallow a holy vow before thinking it through. Proverbs warns that it is a snare to devour what is holy and only afterwards stop to enquire what you have said.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that words spoken to God are not taken back, so I ought to think before I vow.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
